title: WHOSE OPINIONS MATTER? PERSPECTIVE-AWARE MODELS TO IDENTIFY OPINIONS OF HATE SPEECH VICTIMS IN ABUSIVE LANGUAGE DETECTION

bias_targets.methodology: Calculating a Polarization index (P-index) and inter-annotator agreement metrics (e.g., Fleiss' Kappa) to quantify the divergence in subjective hate speech annotations between different demographic groups (e.g., migrants/Muslims vs. local researchers).
Training and evaluating perspective-aware BERT models on Twitter datasets (including a Brexit corpus) to detect anti-immigrant hate speech, racism, aggressiveness, and stereotypes.
Evaluating perspective-aware BERT models on a subset of Brexit Twitter data filtered for Islamophobic content to detect hate speech and offensiveness directed at Muslims.
Training and evaluating perspective-aware BERT classifiers on a Twitter dataset specifically annotated for sexism to detect gender-based abusive language.
Evaluating group-based and inclusive ensemble BERT models on an Italian Twitter dataset to detect homophobic content.
